# Rebuild and trace the displays

```sh
Rscript run_all.R quick
```

The quick route first verifies the release inputs. It then runs the figure scripts in separate R processes and recalculates the selected numerical LaTeX tables with Python's standard library. It writes 18 numerical figures as PDF and PNG, plus 12 LaTeX table files. The conceptual Figure 3 is supplied separately as TeX source.

Each figure script names the CSVs it reads. `manifest/reproduction-map.csv` connects the final manuscript labels to those script and file names. Historical file numbers can differ from the final display number; use the map instead of inferring the number from a filename.

The final approved table fragments are under `verification/tables/`. Some are prose or reference tables. Others were produced by historical aggregations that are not rerun by `quick`. Their inclusion provides an inspectable reference; it does not turn copying a table into recalculating its numbers.

## Inspect a new simulation instead

The quick route always uses the retained paper inputs. To examine your newly generated results, run:

```sh
Rscript run_all.R summarize --study calibration --mode smoke
Rscript run_all.R summarize --study nodes --mode smoke
Rscript run_all.R summarize --study treatment --mode smoke
```

The resulting `summary.csv` stays beside that run. No command silently replaces the retained paper inputs with smoke results. If you extend a design, use its new output for your own analysis and retain its session record.
